Subject: INTERNAL: early findings — KV eviction storm + scheduler backpressure

Karthik / Irene — quick summary from the ops bridge so we can share a concise update with Lily Tech: 

Observations:
- Starting 07:30 EDT, a burst of long-context generations triggered an unusually high prefix cache churn on the us-east-2 inference pool.
- KV cache eviction rate spiked ~6x; some worker processes began returning partial payloads when the KV lookup failed during token streaming (we saw short-lived 'partial write' timeouts).
- Concurrently, the request scheduler mis-attributed available headroom because of a metric aggregation bug (we're tracking the root cause in SUP-9823).

Mitigations applied (in order):
1) Routing policy change -> spill to us-west-1 for new sessions (already active).
2) Temporarily increased prefetch window and disabled aggressive eviction for the us-east-2 pool.
3) Restarted a subset of affected worker hosts running the old scheduler binary to restore stable token streaming.

Next steps:
- Patch scheduler aggregation (I have a PR; will bake in canary and auto-rollback).
- Run a KV eviction throughput test under staged load by 14:00 EDT to validate the config changes.
- Draft a customer-facing incident summary and attach timeline.

Irene, please pull logs for the sample request ids Karthik will collect and escalate if we see other error classes.

Evelyn
VP, Platform Operations

Subject: Post-incident summary & remediation (us-east-2 partial-processing, 2026-09-30)

Jason / Lily Tech support — final update and next steps: 

Summary:
- Impact window: 2026-09-30 07:30–09:05 EDT. Affected customers saw intermittent partial or truncated streaming responses for some generation requests in us-east-2.
- Root cause: a transient KV cache eviction storm combined with a scheduler metric aggregation bug that caused headroom misreporting and resulted in queued workers returning partial streams under specific token-streaming code paths.

Customer impact observed for Lily Tech: approx. 18% truncated responses at peak; reduced to <2% after routing and timeout adjustments.

Remediations completed:
- Immediate: regional fallback routing + increased server-side streaming timeouts (implemented 30 Sep 08:00 EDT).
- Short-term: disabled aggressive KV eviction and restarted impacted workers (30 Sep 08:20–08:45 EDT).
- Code fix: scheduler metric aggregation patch merged and rolled out to canary (01 Oct 11:00 EDT); full rollout scheduled for 01 Oct 18:00 EDT with automatic rollback on latency regressions.
- Monitoring: new alert for KV eviction rate > 3x baseline; expanded tracing to include per-request KV hit/miss histograms.

Preventive actions (tracked items):
- SUP-9823: correct metric aggregation in scheduler (priority: high).
- INF-1147: increase default prefetch window for long-context workloads.
- OPS-567: add early-detection test harness for KV eviction storms.

Attachments: postmortem-draft.docx (customer-facing summary + chronological timeline), incident_timeline.csv (event timestamps and routing changes).

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute wrap-up with your platform team to review the timeline and what the staged rollout means for you. Let me know preferred times and we'll set it up.

Thank you for your patience and for reporting the issue quickly — that helped us converge on the mitigation faster.
